kit/steamgd — Steam transport and invite flow

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Talking to GodotSteam by nameOverlay invite sequenceThe wire is transport-agnosticAPIThe Transport recordWorked example: cavecrawlLive verification

Use kit/steamgd to host and join through Steam lobbies and overlay invites. Friends can select "Join Game" in the overlay without entering an IP address. The package requires the GodotSteam GDExtension's MultiplayerPeer build, which registers both the Steam singleton and SteamMultiplayerPeer class. It supplies a transport beneath kit/netgd's Session_Wire, sharing the session integration used by ENet.

Talking to GodotSteam by name#

The package looks up GodotSteam at runtime through the engine singleton, dynamic object_calls, and ClassDB instantiation. It cannot link at compile time to classes that another extension may not register. This lets the game compile and ship without GodotSteam installed. available() checks for it at runtime, and package procedures safely skip unavailable operations. The same Session_Wire handles either transport.

GodotSteam names are centralized in this module: SINGLETON, PEER_CLASS, and the gd.sname(...) method names. Update those lookups if a supported GodotSteam build changes its API names.

Overlay invite sequence#

The invite-via-overlay flow is:

Code
host:   init(APP_ID) -> create_lobby(max) -> [signal lobby_created] ->
        host_peer(node) -> session_host_start -> invite_overlay(lobby_id)

guest:  friend hits "Join Game" in the Steam overlay ->
        [signal join_requested(lobby_id, friend)] -> join_lobby(lobby_id) ->
        [signal lobby_joined] -> client_peer(node, lobby_owner(lobby_id)) ->
        connected_to_server fires -> the wire's on_net_up joins the session
        exactly like ENet

The wire is transport-agnostic#

Session_Wire listens to SceneMultiplayer's peer_packet, peer_disconnected, connected_to_server, connection_failed, and server_disconnected signals. Replacing ENet's gd.host / gd.join calls with host_peer / client_peer changes the installed MultiplayerPeer while retaining those signals, the four forwarders, the channel plan, and the session.

API#

  • available() -> bool: reports whether GodotSteam is registered in this process. The result does not change during the run.
  • init(app_id := TEST_APP_ID) -> bool: brings Steamworks up (steamInitEx, callbacks embedded in the engine loop). False means Steam is not running, there is no appid, or there is no extension, so show your non-Steam lobby instead. Call once, before any lobby work. TEST_APP_ID is 480 (Spacewar, Valve's test app that every Steamworks account can develop against).
  • listen(node, on_lobby_created := "", on_lobby_joined := "", on_join_requested := "") -> bool: connects GodotSteam's lobby signals to the game's @(gd_method)s (Godot signals must land on script methods, the same contract as netgd.wire_listen). Empty names skip. The handler signatures:
    • on_lobby_created(result: int, lobby_id: int): a result of 1 means success
    • on_lobby_joined(lobby_id: int, perms: int, locked: bool, response: int)
    • on_join_requested(lobby_id: int, friend_id: int): fires when the overlay's "Join Game" button is used
  • create_lobby(max_members := 4, type := Lobby_Type.Friends_Only): the answer arrives on lobby_created. Lobby_Type is Steam's ELobbyType: Private, Friends_Only (the default), Public, or Invisible.
  • join_lobby(lobby_id: u64): the answer arrives on lobby_joined.
  • leave_lobby(lobby_id: u64): releases the one piece of Steam state that outlives the multiplayer peer. Replacing the peer drops its connection but leaves Steam lobby membership active and visible to friends. Call this when returning to the menu or before joining another lobby; it is harmless when not a member.
  • lobby_owner(lobby_id: u64) -> u64: identifies the host of the lobby, the steam id the client peer connects to.
  • my_steam_id() -> u64, persona_name(allocator := context.temp_allocator) -> string: return identity information; the persona name is the natural default for session names.
  • invite_overlay(lobby_id: u64): opens the Steam overlay's invite dialog so players can invite friends to the lobby.
  • host_peer(node: gd.Node) -> bool: installs a Steam host peer on the node's MultiplayerAPI (transport seat 1, like ENet hosting). From here the Session_Wire takes over unchanged.
  • client_peer(node: gd.Node, host_steam_id: u64) -> bool: installs a Steam client peer connected to the lobby owner. connected_to_server fires when the handshake lands, and the wire's on_net_up forward joins the session exactly like ENet.

Both peer procs print an actionable error and return false if SteamMultiplayerPeer isn't registered (i.e. you installed a non-MultiplayerPeer build of GodotSteam).

The Transport record#

ksteam.TRANSPORT implements the netgd.Transport record used by Kit's generic connection helpers:

Odin
// on_lobby_created(result, lobby_id):   host
kboot.boot_open_host(&self.boot, &ksteam.TRANSPORT, {}, name)
ksteam.invite_overlay(u64(lobby_id))

// on_lobby_joined(lobby_id, ...):       guest
kboot.boot_open_join(&self.boot, &ksteam.TRANSPORT, ksteam.endpoint_of(u64(lobby_id)), name, token)

The game still creates and joins lobbies in its Steam signal handlers. Once that lookup completes, pass the resulting Endpoint to the connection helper. endpoint_of(lobby_id) returns {peer_id = lobby_owner(lobby_id)}: Steam connects to the host's Steam id, using the lobby to find it.

Three Transport callbacks are nil in the current Steam integration:

  • pump: the engine polls the peer, like ENet, so there is nothing to pump.
  • close: the peer is replaced by the next install; lobby membership is the part that outlives it, and the lobby id is yours (call leave_lobby).
  • address: there is no verified way to ask which steam id is behind a multiplayer peer. Without a verified mapping, host migration cannot identify a successor. rendezvous is therefore .None, and host migration is disabled on Steam; succession_torch reports this once with the transport name. Some GodotSteam builds expose peer-to-Steam-id mapping, but this repository has not verified it against a running Steam client and extension. Enabling migration requires implementing address against a real build, adding the Rendezvous_Kind branch, and verifying the handoff.

Worked example: cavecrawl#

examples/cavecrawl/scripts/net.odin runs both transports through the same session code. In ready() (cavecrawl.odin), it detects Steam, initializes it, and listens:

Odin
if steamgd.available() && env_int("CAVE_STEAM", 1) != 0 {
	self.steam_on = steamgd.init(env_int("CAVE_APPID", steamgd.TEST_APP_ID))
	if self.steam_on {
		steamgd.listen(self.owner, "on_lobby_created", "on_lobby_joined", "on_join_requested")
	}
}

The Host handler selects the transport. ENet calls gd.host; Steam waits for lobby_created. Both then call the shared begin_hosting session setup. Joining uses the corresponding shared begin_joining procedure.

Odin
@(gd_method)
cave_lobby_on_lobby_created :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby, result: gd.Int, lobby_id: gd.Int) {
	if int(result) != 1 { ... return }
	self.steam_lobby = u64(lobby_id)
	if !steamgd.host_peer(self.owner) { ... return }
	begin_hosting(self)
	steamgd.invite_overlay(self.steam_lobby)
}

lobby_joined also fires when the host joins the lobby it created. Check the lobby owner before creating a client peer so the host does not connect to itself:

Odin
@(gd_method)
cave_lobby_on_lobby_joined :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby, lobby_id: gd.Int, _perms: gd.Int, _locked: gd.Bool, _response: gd.Int) {
	owner := steamgd.lobby_owner(u64(lobby_id))
	if owner == 0 || owner == steamgd.my_steam_id() {
		return // our own lobby (hosts join what they create), or no Steam
	}
	self.steam_lobby = u64(lobby_id)
	if !steamgd.client_peer(self.owner, owner) { ... return }
	// connected_to_server triggers the wire's on_net_up session join.
	begin_joining(self)
}

@(gd_method)
cave_lobby_on_join_requested :: proc(self: ^CaveLobby, lobby_id: gd.Int, _friend: gd.Int) {
	steamgd.join_lobby(u64(lobby_id)) // handles the overlay's "Join Game" request
}

The four wire forwards, wire_attach/wire_listen, kicks, and the latency shim are all identical to the ENet path; see netgd.md.

Live verification#

The Steam connection path requires a running Steam client and cannot be verified by the headless test. To check it live:

  1. Drop the GodotSteam MultiplayerPeer GDExtension into the project (the build that registers SteamMultiplayerPeer, not just the Steam singleton).
  2. Place steam_appid.txt with 480 (Spacewar) next to the binary, or use your real app id.
  3. Use two logged-in Steam accounts that are friends; run host on one, and accept the overlay invite on the other.

Cavecrawl's headless run.sh checks the fallback path: when available() is false, the game uses its non-Steam lobby and logs CAVE_STEAM off. That test does not verify a live Steam connection. Set CAVE_STEAM=0 to disable the Steam path even when GodotSteam is installed.
